records.source: 0 when every value is equal, approaching 1 when one value holds everything. The standard evenness statistic for a pooled library, and the same one :func:`spacr.plot.plot_lorenz_curves` reports.
records.translation: Vale 0 cuando todos los valores son iguales y se aproxima a 1 cuando un solo valor lo acapara todo. Es la estadística de uniformidad habitual para una biblioteca agrupada, y la misma que informa :func:`spacr.plot.plot_lorenz_curves`.

records.context: The statistic is the same but its input is not, although both are labelled "Gini". The Lorenz curves take raw gRNA counts pooled over a laboratory microplate; this panel takes each guide's share of its own well divided by that well's equal split. On the tsg101 screening experiment those are 0.20 and 0.32 -- the panel's is larger because normalising by the well removes the between-well spread that flattens the pooled curve. The two values are therefore not comparable.
records.label: spacr.figures.distributions.gini#2
records.review_basis: Direct AI technical authoring against exact current English source and normal target-neutral context
records.source: The statistic is the same but its input is not, although both are labelled "Gini". The Lorenz curves take raw gRNA counts pooled over a plate; this panel takes each guide's share of its own well divided by that well's equal split. On the tsg101 screen those are 0.20 and 0.32 -- the panel's is larger because normalising by the well removes the between-well spread that flattens the pooled curve. The two values are therefore not comparable.
records.translation: La estadística es la misma, pero su entrada no, aunque ambas lleven la etiqueta "Gini". Las curvas de Lorenz toman recuentos brutos de gRNA agrupados en una placa; este panel toma la proporción de cada guía en su propio pocillo dividida por el reparto equitativo de ese pocillo. En el cribado de tsg101 esos valores son 0.20 y 0.32 -- el del panel es mayor porque normalizar por pocillo elimina la dispersión entre pocillos que aplana la curva agrupada. Por tanto, los dos valores no son comparables.

records.source: The control guides are used first, because the spread of guides that target nothing is the null distribution. With fewer than :data:`MIN_CONTROLS` finite controls, or zero control spread, the MAD of all finite coefficients is used instead. On the reference screen the two agree closely (0.83 against 0.84), but a strong signal raises the all-guide MAD while the control MAD is unchanged.
records.translation: Se usan primero las guías de control, porque la dispersión de las guías que no tienen diana es la distribución nula. Con menos de :data:`MIN_CONTROLS` controles finitos, o con dispersión nula de los controles, se usa en su lugar la MAD de todos los coeficientes finitos. En el cribado de referencia ambas coinciden estrechamente (0.83 frente a 0.84), pero una señal fuerte eleva la MAD de todas las guías mientras que la MAD de los controles no cambia.

records.context: **Unit of replication.** spaCR measures thousands of cells across a handful of microplate sample positions. Testing across cells when the replicate is the microplate sample position is pseudoreplication and can return p < 1e-10 on pure noise, because n is inflated about a thousandfold. Every result states what n counted, and :func:`compare` takes a ``unit`` so a caller can aggregate first.
records.label: spacr.figures.stats#5
records.review_basis: Direct AI technical authoring against exact current English source and normal target-neutral context
records.source: **Unit of replication.** spaCR measures thousands of cells across a handful of wells. Testing across cells when the replicate is the well is pseudoreplication and can return p < 1e-10 on pure noise, because n is inflated about a thousandfold. Every result states what n counted, and :func:`compare` takes a ``unit`` so a caller can aggregate first.
records.translation: **Unidad de replicación.** spaCR mide miles de células en un puñado de pocillos. Realizar la prueba entre células cuando la réplica es el pocillo es pseudorreplicación y puede devolver p < 1e-10 con ruido puro, porque n se infla unas mil veces. Cada resultado indica qué contó n, y :func:`compare` acepta un ``unit`` para que el llamador pueda agregar primero.

records.source: A p-value alone is not reportable. Every result carries the test by name, n per group, an effect size, and the assumption checks with their own numbers.
records.translation: Un p-valor por sí solo no es publicable. Cada resultado incluye la prueba por su nombre, la n de cada grupo, un tamaño del efecto y las comprobaciones de supuestos con sus propios números.

records.source: This is the only module in spaCR that selects a test. :mod:`spacr.sp_stats` previously selected its own and disagreed with this one on three of five inputs, each time choosing the parametric branch where the checks lacked power. It is now a translation layer onto :func:`compare`, :func:`check_normality` and :func:`check_equal_variance` that keeps its older signatures and result keys. Change the choices here and both entry points move together; ``tests/test_one_engine_decides_which_test_applies.py`` fails if they ever come apart again.
records.translation: Este es el único módulo de spaCR que selecciona una prueba. :mod:`spacr.sp_stats` seleccionaba antes la suya propia y discrepaba de este en tres de cinco entradas, eligiendo cada vez la rama paramétrica cuando las comprobaciones carecían de potencia. Ahora es una capa de traducción sobre :func:`compare`, :func:`check_normality` y :func:`check_equal_variance` que conserva sus firmas y claves de resultado anteriores. Si se cambian aquí las elecciones, ambos puntos de entrada cambian a la vez; ``tests/test_one_engine_decides_which_test_applies.py`` falla si vuelven a separarse.

A labels mask may be at full resolution while a downsampled preview is not; a points layer of centroids is in continuous coordinates and has no grid at all; and confocal z-stacks in this codebase are routinely anisotropic — 0.65 µm in x and y, 2 µm in z is an ordinary spaCR stack.

records.source: Layers do not agree on pixels. A labels mask may be at full resolution while a downsampled preview is not; a points layer of centroids is in continuous coordinates and has no grid at all; and confocal z-stacks in this codebase are routinely anisotropic — 0.65 µm in x and y, 2 µm in z is an ordinary spaCR stack.
records.translation: Las capas no coinciden en los píxeles. Una máscara de etiquetas puede estar a resolución completa mientras que una vista previa submuestreada no; una capa de puntos de centroides está en coordenadas continuas y no tiene ninguna cuadrícula; y las pilas z confocales de este código son habitualmente anisótropas — 0.65 µm en x e y, 2 µm en z es una pila de spaCR corriente.

records.context: So a layer never says "row 40, column 12". It says "this data axis is *z*, one step along it is 2 µm, and element 0 sits at 0 µm" — a :class:`Spacing` — and everything downstream happens in world units. A :class:`Canvas` is a window onto that world (an origin, a step and a size, over two named world axes), and rendering is: for every canvas pixel, ask each layer what is at that world coordinate.
records.label: spacr.layers#9
records.review_basis: Direct AI technical authoring against exact current English source and normal target-neutral context
records.source: So a layer never says "row 40, column 12". It says "this data axis is *z*, one step along it is 2 µm, and element 0 sits at 0 µm" — a :class:`Spacing` — and everything downstream happens in world units. A :class:`Canvas` is a window onto that world (an origin, a step and a size, over two named world axes), and rendering is: for every canvas pixel, ask each layer what is at that world coordinate.
records.translation: Por eso una capa nunca dice "row 40, column 12" (fila 40, columna 12). Dice "este eje de datos es *z*, un paso a lo largo de él mide 2 µm y el elemento 0 está en 0 µm" — un :class:`Spacing` — y todo lo posterior ocurre en unidades del mundo. Un :class:`Canvas` es una ventana a ese mundo (un origen, un paso y un tamaño, sobre dos ejes del mundo con nombre), y representar consiste en preguntar a cada capa, para cada píxel del lienzo, qué hay en esa coordenada del mundo.

records.source: Five modes, all of which honour ``opacity`` the same way — ``alpha = coverage * opacity`` — except :data:`OPAQUE`, which first sets every non-zero coverage to 1, so a soft-edged layer fully covers the layers below it wherever it has any coverage. Opacity still scales an opaque layer; "opaque" describes what it does to the layers below it where it *has* something, not whether it can be faded.
records.translation: Cinco modos, todos los cuales respetan ``opacity`` de la misma manera — ``alpha = coverage * opacity`` — excepto :data:`OPAQUE`, que primero fija en 1 toda cobertura distinta de cero, de modo que una capa de bordes suaves cubre por completo las capas inferiores allí donde tiene alguna cobertura. records.source: **Names are unique.** A duplicate name means "hide the mask" hides the wrong one. Colliding names are suffixed rather than refused, because a user adding a second mask should get one, not an error dialog.
records.translation: **Los nombres son únicos.** Un nombre duplicado significa que "hide the mask" (ocultar la máscara) oculta la equivocada. A los nombres que colisionan se les añade un sufijo en lugar de rechazarlos, porque un usuario que añade una segunda máscara debe obtenerla, no un diálogo de error.

records.source: **Units agree.** A layer measured in µm and a layer measured in pixels cannot be composited: the numbers would line up and the picture would not. Mixing them raises rather than drawing something plausible.

records.translation: **El valor predeterminado, REPLACE, actualiza en el propio objeto:** se sobrescribe el valor de una MapAnnotation existente cuyo espacio de nombres es exactamente el de spaCR. records.context: **TagAnnotations are never edited.** In OMERO a tag is a *shared* object; renaming the tag linked to this image renames it on every other object in the group that carries it. So :func:`export_tag_annotation` links a tag when the verdict is new, does nothing when the identical verdict is already linked, and reports the previous tag when the verdict has *changed* — it never unlinks and never renames.

records.translation: **Las TagAnnotations nunca se editan.** En OMERO una etiqueta es un objeto *compartido*; renombrar la etiqueta vinculada a esta imagen la renombra en todos los demás objetos del grupo que la llevan. Por eso :func:`export_tag_annotation` vincula una etiqueta cuando el veredicto es nuevo, no hace nada cuando el veredicto idéntico ya está vinculado, e informa de la etiqueta anterior cuando el veredicto ha *cambiado* — nunca desvincula ni renombra.

records.context: This module is called ``spacr/omero.py`` and does not shadow the third-party ``omero`` package. Absolute imports have been the default since Python 3, so a module inside the ``spacr`` package that asks for ``omero`` gets the top-level distribution, not its own sibling. That is verified rather than assumed — see ``tests/test_omero.py::test_spacr_omero_does_not_shadow_the_third_party_package``, which puts a decoy ``omero`` package on ``sys.path`` and checks which one arrives — because a self-import here would be silent and would look like a broken OMERO install.

records.source: This module is called ``spacr/omero.py`` and does not shadow the third-party ``omero`` package. Absolute imports have been the default since Python 3, so a module inside the ``spacr`` package that asks for ``omero`` gets the top-level distribution, not its own sibling. That is verified rather than assumed — see ``tests/test_omero.py::test_spacr_omero_does_not_shadow_the_third_party_package``, which puts a decoy ``omero`` package on ``sys.path`` and checks which one arrives — because a self-import here would be silent and would look like a broken OMERO install.
records.translation: Este módulo se llama ``spacr/omero.py`` y no oculta el paquete de terceros ``omero``. Las importaciones absolutas son el comportamiento predeterminado desde Python 3, de modo que un módulo dentro del paquete ``spacr`` que pide ``omero`` obtiene la distribución de nivel superior, no su propio módulo hermano. Esto se verifica en lugar de suponerse — véase ``tests/test_omero.py::test_spacr_omero_does_not_shadow_the_third_party_package``, que coloca un paquete señuelo ``omero`` en ``sys.path`` y comprueba cuál llega —, porque una autoimportación aquí sería silenciosa y parecería una instalación de OMERO rota.

records.context: The import is written as ``importlib.import_module(OMERO_GATEWAY_MODULE)`` rather than as a literal ``import omero.gateway`` for that same reason: the one place the name is resolved is a named constant next to the guard that checks what came back, instead of a bare statement in a file of the same name. The cost is that ``tests/test_declared_dependencies_match_imports.py`` — which reads import *statements* out of the AST — cannot see it, exactly as it cannot see ``umap``. That blind spot is pinned from the other side by ``tests/test_omero.py::test_omero_py_is_reached_through_a_string_literal_and_must_not_be_removed``, so a dependency audit does not report omero-py as unused.

records.translation: Es exactamente :func:`spacr.convert.target_name` — la forma exacta que analiza ``spacr.utils._get_regex('cellvoyager', 'tif')`` —, de modo que la carpeta de salida se entrega directamente a Mask/Measure con ``metadata_type='cellvoyager'`` y nada más. **Aquí no se inventa ninguna disposición nueva.** Lo único que debe sobrevivir al trayecto es la geometría de la placa, porque spaCR indexa cada medición, cada gráfico y cada estadística a nivel de pocillo mediante ``plateID`` / ``rowID`` / ``columnID`` / ``fieldID``; :func:`well_position` es donde el ``(row, column)`` basado en 0 de OMERO se convierte en el ``('r1', 'c1')`` de spaCR y en el nombre de pocillo ``A01``.

records.context: Everything that is easy to get wrong here is *arithmetic and string formatting*, not RPC: the row/column mapping, the filename, the id parsing, the float formatting, the decision to replace rather than append. All of it lives in pure functions over plain data — :func:`well_position`, :func:`plane_filename`, :func:`parse_object_ref`, :func:`format_map_value`, :func:`measurement_pairs`, :func:`plan_annotation` — and the ``BlitzGateway`` calls are confined to a thin layer that only walks containers and moves bytes. This module is therefore tested on a machine with no OMERO server and no ``omero-py`` installed: the fake gateway in ``tests/test_omero.py`` implements about a dozen methods, and everything worth testing is reachable through it.

records.review_basis: Direct AI technical authoring against exact current English source and normal target-neutral context
records.source: Everything that is easy to get wrong here is *arithmetic and string formatting*, not RPC: the row/column mapping, the filename, the id parsing, the float formatting, the decision to replace rather than append. All of it lives in pure functions over plain data — :func:`well_position`, :func:`plane_filename`, :func:`parse_object_ref`, :func:`format_map_value`, :func:`measurement_pairs`, :func:`plan_annotation` — and the ``BlitzGateway`` calls are confined to a thin layer that only walks containers and moves bytes. This module is therefore tested on a machine with no OMERO server and no ``omero-py`` installed: the fake gateway in ``tests/test_omero.py`` implements about a dozen methods, and everything worth testing is reachable through it.
records.translation: Todo lo que aquí es fácil hacer mal es *aritmética y formateo de cadenas*, no RPC: la correspondencia de filas y columnas, el nombre de archivo, el análisis de los id, el formateo de números de coma flotante, la decisión de sustituir en lugar de añadir. Todo ello reside en funciones puras sobre datos simples — :func:`well_position`, :func:`plane_filename`, :func:`parse_object_ref`, :func:`format_map_value`, :func:`measurement_pairs`, :func:`plan_annotation` — y las llamadas a ``BlitzGateway`` se limitan a una capa fina que solo recorre contenedores y mueve bytes. Por eso este módulo se prueba en una máquina sin servidor OMERO y sin ``omero-py`` instalado: la pasarela falsa de ``tests/test_omero.py`` implementa una docena de métodos, y todo lo que merece la pena probar es accesible a través de ella.

records.context: **Why there is a cap.** A spaCR object table has 300-600 columns. A MapAnnotation with 400 entries renders in OMERO.web as a 400-row scrolling table in a 300 px panel, which hides the annotations worth showing. So the annotation is a *summary*, capped at ``max_pairs`` (:data:`MAX_MAP_PAIRS` = 50 by default) and ordered so the useful structured-data names are the ones that survive: ``priority`` structured-data names first in the order given, then the row's own order. When anything is cut, the last pair is :data:`TRUNCATION_KEY`, saying how many were dropped and that the full table is the CSV attached under :data:`NS_FILE`. The full table is never *only* in the annotation.

records.source: **Why there is a cap.** A spaCR object table has 300-600 columns. A MapAnnotation with 400 entries renders in OMERO.web as a 400-row scrolling table in a 300 px panel, which hides the annotations worth showing. So the annotation is a *summary*, capped at ``max_pairs`` (:data:`MAX_MAP_PAIRS` = 50 by default) and ordered so the useful keys are the ones that survive: ``priority`` keys first in the order given, then the row's own order. When anything is cut, the last pair is :data:`TRUNCATION_KEY`, saying how many were dropped and that the full table is the CSV attached under :data:`NS_FILE`. The full table is never *only* in the annotation.
records.translation: **Por qué hay un límite.** Una tabla de objetos de spaCR tiene 300-600 columnas. Una MapAnnotation con 400 entradas se muestra en OMERO.web como una tabla desplazable de 400 filas en un panel de 300 px, lo que oculta las anotaciones que merece la pena mostrar. Por eso la anotación es un *resumen*, limitado a ``max_pairs`` (:data:`MAX_MAP_PAIRS` = 50 de forma predeterminada) y ordenado para que las claves útiles sean las que se conservan: primero las claves de ``priority`` en el orden indicado y después el orden propio de la fila. Cuando se recorta algo, el último par es :data:`TRUNCATION_KEY`, que indica cuántos se descartaron y que la tabla completa es el CSV adjunto bajo :data:`NS_FILE`. La tabla completa nunca está *solo* en la anotación.

records.context: Under :data:`REPLACE` — the default — an annotation whose namespace is *exactly* ``namespace`` is updated in place. Nothing is created, nothing is unlinked and **nothing is deleted**; a re-run therefore leaves one annotation rather than a growing pile, and an annotation in any other namespace (a colleague's, OMERO's own bulk annotations) is never even considered. When more than one already exists — only possible after an :data:`APPEND` run or a concurrent writer — the oldest (lowest id) is updated and the rest are reported in ``duplicates`` rather than removed, because an annotation may be linked elsewhere.

records.source: Under :data:`REPLACE` — the default — an annotation whose namespace is *exactly* ``namespace`` is updated in place. Nothing is created, nothing is unlinked and **nothing is deleted**; a re-run therefore leaves one annotation rather than a growing pile, and an annotation in any other namespace (a colleague's, OMERO's own bulk annotations) is never even considered. When more than one already exists — only possible after an :data:`APPEND` run or a concurrent writer — the oldest (lowest id) is updated and the rest are reported in ``duplicates`` rather than removed, because an annotation may be linked elsewhere.
records.translation: Con :data:`REPLACE` — el valor predeterminado —, una anotación cuyo espacio de nombres es *exactamente* ``namespace`` se actualiza en el propio objeto. No se crea nada, no se desvincula nada y **no se elimina nada**; por tanto, una nueva ejecución deja una sola anotación en lugar de un montón creciente, y una anotación de cualquier otro espacio de nombres (la de un colega, las anotaciones masivas propias de OMERO) ni siquiera se tiene en cuenta. Cuando ya existe más de una — algo solo posible tras una ejecución con :data:`APPEND` o con un escritor concurrente —, se actualiza la más antigua (el id más bajo) y las demás se notifican en ``duplicates`` en lugar de eliminarse, porque una anotación puede estar vinculada en otro lugar.

records.context: The mean of each numeric column over the rows that actually have a value there, plus ``n_objects``. Missing values are *excluded from their own column's mean* rather than zero-filled: in spaCR a NaN is usually structural (a ``pathogen_*`` column is NaN for a cell with no pathogen in it), and zero-filling turns "no pathogen" into "a pathogen of zero size". A column with no usable value in any row is reported as ``None``, which :func:`measurement_pairs` renders as ``NaN``.

records.source: The mean of each numeric column over the rows that actually have a value there, plus ``n_objects``. Missing values are *excluded from their own column's mean* rather than zero-filled: in spaCR a NaN is usually structural (a ``pathogen_*`` column is NaN for a cell with no pathogen in it), and zero-filling turns "no pathogen" into "a pathogen of zero size". A column with no usable value in any row is reported as ``None``, which :func:`measurement_pairs` renders as ``NaN``.
records.translation: La media de cada columna numérica sobre las filas que realmente tienen un valor en ella, más ``n_objects``. Los valores ausentes se *excluyen de la media de su propia columna* en lugar de rellenarse con cero: en spaCR un NaN suele ser estructural (una columna ``pathogen_*`` es NaN para una célula sin patógeno), y rellenar con cero convierte "no pathogen" (sin patógeno) en "un patógeno de tamaño cero". Una columna sin ningún valor utilizable en ninguna fila se informa como ``None``, que :func:`measurement_pairs` representa como ``NaN``.
